items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: So that wound up with Wilmer Breaux, Sugar Johnny, Lawrence Dewey, Roy Palmer, myself and Lil Hardin.

ctx.x: You were too young to get them involved.

Yeah, I wasn't quite old enough yet for the first draft. So when he went, I'd taken over, and in the meantime, I don't know what happened to Tuley Garland, but when I wound up, Breaux was playing bass, Wilmer Breaux. So that wound up with Wilmer Breaux, Sugar Johnny, Lawrence Dewey, Roy Palmer, myself and Lil Hardin. See, she was then Hardin, it wasn't Armstrong's right there. There's a picture, I've seen that picture of that band. Yeah, that's right. So we made it so good up there, at the meantime, Sugar Johnny…

items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: Yeah. So after Sugar died, I think if I'm not mistaken, I don't know who was playing trumpet.

ctx.x: I guess that was his girlfriend for a while.

Yeah. So after Sugar died, I think if I'm not mistaken, I don't know who was playing trumpet. Well anyhow, no that's right, they got in Mud Carey, that's right. Mud Carey came in there once. That's right. Mud Carey came in there. And Johnny Dodds came up there together. Yeah. I don't know how the mix up come up, but it was at the Dreamland, then the band changed a little. Papa Mud was playing trumpet and Dodds was playing clarinet then. So at the meantime, Papa Mud wanted to take a trip back to New Orleans. So…
